# Implement Milestone 4 locally

Run in the full jpdevpersonal/trading-platform VS Code checkout. When the owner invokes this prompt approving the recommended US/Massive scope, proceed with implementation. If the owner specifies a different market or provider, identify the affected decisions and resolve those before building the adapter. Do not require a live key to build or run the deterministic tests.

Use [the M04 specification](../../docs/milestones/04-daily-price-history.md), its 20 required acceptance IDs, [provider decision](../../docs/milestones/04-market-data-providers.md) and [verification checklist](../../docs/milestones/04-daily-price-history-verification.md). Read these files from disk if links fail to resolve.

1. **Inspect the checkout.** Read [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md), [Copilot guidance](../copilot-instructions.md), [requirements](../../docs/requirements.md), [architecture](../../docs/architecture.md), [ADR 0001](../../docs/decisions/0001-local-first-modular-monolith.md), [standards](../../docs/engineering-standards.md), [milestone index](../../docs/milestones.md), [M03 verification](../../docs/milestones/03-backend-api-and-database-verification.md), and [README](../../README.md). Record status, origin identity (redacted), HEAD and ancestry against 9259f496f82d12fab7e3d725edac2a070e310cd6. Review later changes. Work on a local M04 branch based on compatible merged main. Preserve unrelated edits and these planning files. Add the M04 link to the index without overwriting earlier entries. Outline the phases and checks; then do the work. Raise material architecture conflicts before changing affected code.
2. **Build persistence and listing setup.** Inspect the actual M03 model, migration, context, integration fixtures and SQL seed. Add the additive daily-bar and refresh schema and the separate opt-in real-listing script. Generate and inspect the migration with the pinned EF tool. Verify fresh and M03 upgrade paths on disposable PostgreSQL. Preserve prior fixtures and catalogue contracts. Prove composite uniqueness, concurrent imports, correction handling, unaffected dates, exact decimals and rollback with focused tests.
3. **Implement import and read.** Keep Domain independent and ports/use cases in Application. Put Massive HTTP and PostgreSQL in Infrastructure; keep transport and DI in API. Implement the exact routes, source/date semantics, bounded requests, cancellation, quota and safe errors in the spec. Reuse existing validation, CORS origins, logging and readiness conventions. Add only the browser POST capabilities required here. Keep keys backend-only, redact diagnostics, and keep GET independent of provider availability. Test requests against a controlled HTTP handler with synthetic envelopes and test DB/HTTP using the existing real-Postgres harness.
4. **Connect the browser.** Build /price-history in the existing shell and link it from Dashboard. Use a typed API client, existing paged catalogue, explicit manual import, accessible keyboard controls and the source-labelled chronological table (newest first). Preserve selection and range on reload. Distinguish latest session from last successful stock refresh. Test no-key reads, empty/error states, retry, throttling and stale responses. Leave the existing previews usable.
5. **Verify the assembled feature.** Run the checklist in full. Add a deterministic Playwright journey through real frontend → real ASP.NET API → real PostgreSQL with only Massive simulated through test wiring. Do not make public provider calls in CI, add a fake fallback to the production path, or count network mocking at the browser/API boundary as full-workflow evidence. Keep the existing preview smoke suite independent of PostgreSQL. Wire the new test into the existing PR verification and document its local command. Where an authorized local key is available, run the live walkthrough. Otherwise mark M04-LIVE-001 Blocked with its exact remaining check and finish the rest.
6. **Report against all 20 IDs.** Update the runbook with setup, explicit migration, listing setup, provider configuration, import/read contract, sample vs real data, limits and recovery. Fill in the checklist with actual commands, counts and evidence, including failures and retries. Record hosted job and owner review only if observed. Finish with a concise description of what the owner can do in the browser, which IDs remain open and why. Leave pushes, PR submission, merges and deployment to the owner. No broker integration, orders, background refresh, charts, paid services or other milestones.
